questions.text: As per the Basel III Capital Regulations implemented by the RBI for Scheduled Commercial Banks (excluding Regional Rural Banks and Payments Banks), what is the prescribed level of Capital Conservation Buffer (CCB) as a percentage of Risk Weighted Assets (RWAs)?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Basel III standard CCB is universally 2.5%. India adopted the full Basel III framework. The Countercyclical Capital Buffer (CCyB) varies (0-2.5%), but CCB is fixed at 2.5%. Full Solution: The RBI's Master Circular on Basel III Capital Regulations mandates a Capital Conservation Buffer (CCB) of 2.5% of RWAs, to be met entirely with Common Equity Tier 1 (CET1) capital. This is over and above the minimum CET1 requirement of 5.5% and minimum Total Capital requirement of 9%, bringing the effective Total Capital + CCB requirement to 11.5%.

questions.text: A car travels from city X to city Y at a speed of 40 km/h and returns from Y to X at 60 km/h. What is the average speed for the entire round trip?
questions.solution: Shortcut: For equal distances, average speed is the harmonic mean = 2ab/(a+b) = 2×40×60/(40+60) = 48 km/h. Full method: Let one-way distance be d. Time onward = d/40, return = d/60. Total distance = 2d, total time = d/40 + d/60 = 5d/120 = d/24. Average speed = 2d ÷ (d/24) = 48 km/h.

questions.text: Under the Pradhan Mantri Mudra Yojana (PMMY), loans are classified into three categories — 'Shishu', 'Kishor', and 'Tarun' — based on the loan amount. What is the applicable loan range for the 'Tarun' category?
questions.solution: Shortcut (Elimination): Memorize the ascending order: Shishu (Child) → Kishor (Adolescent) → Tarun (Adult). Option D (Up to ₹50,000) is the 'Shishu' limit. Option B (₹50k–₹5L) is the 'Kishor' limit. Option D (₹10L–₹20L) exceeds the PMMY cap of ₹10L (relevant for Stand Up India). The only remaining range for the top category 'Tarun' is Option C (₹5L–₹10L). Step-by-step: PMMY offers loans up to ₹10 Lakh. 'Shishu' covers loans up to ₹50,000. 'Kishor' covers loans above ₹50,000 up to ₹5,00,000. 'Tarun' covers loans above ₹5,00,000 up to ₹10,00,000.

questions.text: In the following question, a word is given followed by four sentences. Choose the sentence in which the usage of the word is INCORRECT or INAPPROPRIATE. WORD: PRECLUDE

options.label: A
options.text: The new regulations preclude the possibility of early withdrawal without a penalty.

options.label: B
options.text: His lack of experience does not preclude him from applying for the senior position.

options.label: C
options.text: The heavy rainfall precluded the match from being played on schedule.

options.label: D
options.text: The contract precludes the company to share data with third parties.

questions.solution: Shortcut: Scan options for the pattern 'Preclude + Object + To + Verb'. The verb 'preclude' strictly follows the pattern 'Preclude + Object + From + Gerund' or takes a direct noun object. 'Preclude to [verb]' is always wrong. Step-by-step: Option A uses 'preclude' with a noun object ('possibility') — correct. Option B uses 'preclude him from applying' (Object + from + gerund) — correct. Option C uses 'precluded the match from being played' — correct. Option D uses 'precludes the company to share', violating the required 'from sharing' structure. Hence, Option D is incorrect.

questions.text: Read the sentence to find out whether there is any grammatical error in it. The error, if any, will be in one part of the sentence. The letter of that part is the answer. If there is no error, the answer is 'No Error'. (Ignore errors of punctuation, if any.) The rapid pace of technological change (A) / have rendered many traditional (B) / banking models obsolete, forcing (C) / institutions to adapt quickly to survive. (D) / No Error (E)
questions.solution: Shortcut: Ignore the prepositional phrase 'of technological change' between the subject 'Pace' (singular) and the verb. The singular subject 'Pace' requires the singular verb 'has rendered', not 'have rendered'. Step-by-step: The core subject is 'The rapid pace' (singular). The phrase 'of technological change' modifies 'pace' but does not change its number. Therefore, the verb must be singular ('has rendered'). Part B uses the plural verb 'have rendered', creating a subject-verb agreement error. Parts A, C, and D are grammatically correct.

questions.text: Eight people (P, Q, R, S, T, U, V, W) are to be seated around a circular table. Q sits immediately to the right of P. R sits opposite to S. T does not sit next to U. If P occupies the northmost seat, which of the following could be the person sitting at the south‑west position?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Visualise the circle as a clock. Place P at 12 o'clock; Q must be at 1 o'clock (right of P). Opposite seats are 6 hours apart, so S is opposite R. Try placements quickly: put R at 6 o'clock, then S at 12 (conflict with P). So R cannot be at 6. Place R at 3 o'clock, then S at 9 o'clock. This leaves seats 5,7,11,12 for the rest, respecting T‑U restriction. The south‑west position corresponds to 7 o'clock, which can be occupied by W without breaking any rule. Full solution: By systematic trial respecting all constraints, the only feasible occupant for the 7‑o'clock seat is W.

questions.text: What is the unit digit of (7^2023 + 3^2024)?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Unit digits of powers repeat every 4. 2023 mod 4 = 3 → 7^3 ends with 3. 2024 mod 4 = 0 → 3^4 ends with 1. Sum of unit digits = 3 + 1 = 4.

questions.text: In a family relationship code: 'X @ Y' means X is the mother of Y; 'X # Y' means X is the brother of Y; 'X $ Y' means X is the aunt of Y; 'X % Y' means X is the son of Y. If the statement "M % N @ O # P $ Q" is true, what is the relationship between M and Q?

options.label: A
options.text: M is the nephew of Q

options.label: B
options.text: M is the grandson of Q

options.label: C
options.text: M is the brother‑in‑law of Q

options.label: D
options.text: M is the son‑in‑law of Q

questions.solution: Shortcut: Work from right to left, replacing each symbol with its meaning. Q is aunt of P ($), so P is nephew of Q. P is brother of O (#), so O is also nephew of Q. O is mother of N (@), so N is child of O, i.e., also nephew of Q. Finally, M is son of N (%), making M a grandson of Q. Full solution: Stepwise translation gives Q (aunt) → P (nephew) → O (brother of P, also nephew) → N (child of O, still nephew) → M (son of N) = grandson of Q.

questions.text: Under the Pradhan Mantri Kisan Samman Nidhi (PM-KISAN) scheme, what is the total annual financial benefit provided to eligible landholding farmer families, and in how many equal installments is it disbursed?
questions.solution: Shortcut: PM-KISAN provides Rs. 6,000/year. The amount is split into three equal installments of Rs. 2,000 each (April-July, August-November, December-March). Eliminate options with wrong amounts (10k, 12k) or wrong frequency (2, 4). Full Solution: The PM-KISAN scheme, launched in 2019, provides income support of Rs. 6,000 per year to all landholding farmer families. The amount is released in three equal installments of Rs. 2,000 every four months directly into the bank accounts of beneficiaries via Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT).

questions.text: Under the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934 (as amended by the Finance Act, 2016), what is the minimum quorum required for a meeting of the Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) and who exercises the casting vote in case of a tie?

options.label: A
options.text: Quorum: 4 members; Casting Vote: RBI Governor

options.label: B
options.text: Quorum: 4 members; Casting Vote: External Member elected by majority

options.label: C
options.text: Quorum: 5 members; Casting Vote: RBI Governor

options.label: D
options.text: Quorum: 3 members; Casting Vote: Senior-most Deputy Governor

questions.solution: Shortcut: MPC has 6 members; quorum is typically majority (4). The Governor is the ex-officio Chairperson and holds the casting vote. Eliminate options with 3 or 5 quorum and non-Governor casting votes. Full Solution: Section 45ZB(4) of the RBI Act stipulates that four members shall constitute the quorum for an MPC meeting. Section 45ZC(2) provides that the Governor shall have a casting vote in case of an equality of votes. The MPC comprises six members (three RBI officials, including the Governor, and three external members).

questions.text: Statements: 1. No politician is a scientist. 2. Some scientists are teachers. 3. All teachers are politicians. Which of the following conclusions is logically valid?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Draw a quick Venn diagram. Place 'politician' and 'scientist' as non‑overlapping sets (statement 1). Since all teachers are politicians (statement 3), teachers lie inside the politician circle, thus cannot intersect scientists. Statement 2 tells us some scientists are teachers, which contradicts the diagram, so the only way to keep consistency is to conclude that the some‑scientists‑are‑teachers must be outside the politician set, meaning those scientists are not teachers. Hence the only unavoidable truth is that some scientists are not politicians. Full solution: From 1, Politician ∩ Scientist = Ø. From 3, Teacher ⊆ Politician, so Teacher ∩ Scientist = Ø. Statement 2 says Some Scientist are Teachers, which can hold only if the 'some' refers to scientists outside the Politician set, implying those scientists are not politicians. Therefore, "Some scientists are not politicians" follows.

questions.text: In the following alphanumeric series, each term follows a specific pattern. Find the missing term. Z1A, X4D, V9G, T16J, ?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Decompose each term into three independent sequences. 1st letters: Z, X, V, T (decreasing by 2 in alphabet) → R. Numbers: 1, 4, 9, 16 (squares of 1, 2, 3, 4) → 25. 3rd letters: A, D, G, J (increasing by 3) → M. Combined: R25M. Full Solution: The first letters are alternate letters from the end of the alphabet: Z(26), X(24), V(22), T(20); the next is R(18). The numerical parts are perfect squares: 1², 2², 3², 4²; the next is 5² = 25. The last letters move forward by 3 positions each time: A(1), D(4), G(7), J(10); the next is M(13). Thus, the missing term is R25M.

questions.text: In a coded blood relation language, 'A @ B' means 'A is the father of B'; 'A # B' means 'A is the sister of B'; 'A $ B' means 'A is the wife of B'; 'A % B' means 'A is the son of B'. If the expression 'P % Q @ R # S $ T' is true, how is P related to T?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Track generation gaps (+1 for @, -1 for %, 0 for #/$) and genders. P % Q (-1, Male), Q @ R (+1, Male), R # S (0, Female), S $ T (0, Female). Net gap = 0 (Same generation). P is Male, T is Male (Husband of S). P is son of Q; Q is father of R & S; S is wife of T. Thus P is brother of S, making P the brother-in-law of T. Step-by-step: 1. P % Q → P is son of Q (P Male, Gen -1). 2. Q @ R → Q is father of R (Q Male, Gen +1 from R). So P, R siblings. 3. R # S → R is sister of S (R, S Females, Same Gen). So P, R, S siblings. 4. S $ T → S is wife of T (T Male, Same Gen). 5. P (Brother of S) → Brother-in-law of T.

questions.text: As per the RBI Guidelines for 'On Tap' Licensing of Small Finance Banks (SFBs) in the Private Sector (December 2019), what is the minimum paid-up voting equity capital or net worth required to set up a Small Finance Bank?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Eliminate Rs. 100 crore (Payments Banks), Rs. 500 crore (Universal Banks old requirement), and Rs. 300 crore (distractor). The specific 'On Tap' SFB licensing guideline mandates a minimum net worth of Rs. 200 crore. Full Solution: The RBI's 'Guidelines for On Tap Licensing of Small Finance Banks in the Private Sector' dated December 5, 2019, explicitly states in Para 4 that the minimum paid-up voting equity capital/net worth required is Rs. 200 crore. This distinguishes SFBs from Payments Banks (Rs. 100 crore) and Universal Banks.

questions.text: As per the Reserve Bank of India's Basel III Framework on Liquidity Standards (2014, updated 2020), Scheduled Commercial Banks (excluding RRBs and Payments Banks) are required to maintain a minimum Liquidity Coverage Ratio (LCR). What is the current minimum LCR requirement (as a percentage of High Quality Liquid Assets to Total Net Cash Outflows)?
questions.solution: Shortcut (Elimination/Regulatory Milestone): LCR was phased in from 60% (2015) to 100% (2019) in steps of 10%. The final steady-state requirement is 100%. Option A (90%) was the 2018 interim step. Option B (110%) and D (125%) are distractors often confused with NSFR (100%) or Capital Adequacy buffers. The standard global and domestic final norm is 100%. Step-by-step: The LCR requires banks to hold HQLA sufficient to survive a 30-day stress scenario. RBI mandated the phase-in: 60% (Jan 2015), 70% (Jan 2016), 80% (Jan 2017), 90% (Jan 2018), 100% (Jan 2019). Since Jan 2019, the minimum requirement is 100%.
